headline: No documented interaction pathway; both open-source data-engineering profiles show no network egress or I/O surfaces, so pairwise risks are mostly blocked by missing surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes a shared channel, filesystem, or parser surface that would let one agent inject instructions into the other. agent_a has no io_surfaces and network_egress is none; agent_b likewise has no io_surfaces and network_egress is none. With no documented bridge, prompt injection is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles show no data classes touched, no shared workspace, and no network egress for either agent, so there is no plausible leakage path from one to the other in the documented setup. Because both are docs-only and unverified, I do not infer hidden storage or upload behavior.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or external upload path is added for either agent, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep both agents offline from external services.
requires-engineering: add explicit data-class allowlists before enabling storage access.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented for either agent: both profiles have empty io_surfaces and no concurrency model. Without filesystem, network, or mutable-resource access, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate between agent_a and agent_b.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or mutable service, conflict risk becomes relevant.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for both agents.
Separate any future mutable resources by agent.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if shared writes are enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pathway where agent_a's output becomes authoritative input for agent_b, and neither profile shows action-taking authority. With no I/O surfaces and no evidence of downstream automation, cascading error is not plausible in the current pair.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to consume agent_a outputs as trusted inputs, cascading error risk must be reassessed.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing outputs.
Do not chain the agents in an automated pipeline.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles touch no data classes. Since the compliance rubric depends on actual data flow or policy mismatch, there is no evidenced compliance breach to score here.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance controls must be checked against the new handling policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document residency and retention before any deployment.
requires-engineering: perform a policy review if data handling changes.
